newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends down after recovery falters.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends down after recovery falters.

text.p: IPE December Brent closed down and just 11 cents off the day's lows on Thursday after a late recovery that trimmed sharp mid-morning losses ran out of steam, traders said.
December Brent closed down 32 cents at $23.76 a barrel after a flurry of late selling closed out a featureless late afternoon and continued a shakeout of long positions built up in the autumn rally.
"It's finished absolutely dead. We've ended up pretty much where we started the day," said one trader.
The NYMEX heating oil contract also closed down, at 70.50 cents a gallon.
Traders said the market was helped lower by reports of additional cargoes of heating oil coming from the U.S. and the Mediterranean and continuing mild weather in Europe.
Dec Brent has shed around $1 since Tuesday's close while Nov gas oil has dropped more than $10 amid bearish reaction to big builds in heating oil stocks in the U.S. Northeast.
High productivity at European and U.S. refineries with a view to replenishing heating fuels stocks ahead of the winter has also taking some of the edge off the recent rally.
IPE November gas oil closed down $2.00 a tonne at $223.50 on Thursday, having climbed back from lows of $219.50.
"It's a struggling recovery, a thin scramble and not the best version -- it didn't bounce particularly quickly after opening low," said one trader.
Dealers though Brent might still make up further ground, with $23.90 a barrel seen as a swing point dividing the morning trader from afternoon business.
"The night is young for Brent, but it's not a bandwagon to jump on," one trader said.
